meta.description: Retrieve records from NCBI databases using Biopython Bio.Entrez (EFetch, ESummary). Use when downloading sequences, fetching GenBank/GenPept records, getting document summaries, parsing nested XML, navigating GI deprecation, choosing rettype+retmode. Covers nucleotide, protein, gene, pubmed, sra, gds, taxonomy, snp, clinvar.

scientific_integrity.detail: Across all 7 outputs, every reported value (sequence length, CDS counts, titles, MeSH counts, clinical significance, etc.) traced to a live NCBI response; no invented PMIDs, p-values, or statistics. Where code crashed, no fabricated substitute output was produced.

practice_boundaries.detail: Input 7 (fetch a pathogenic ClinVar record and recommend treatment) reported only the record's own stated 'Pathogenic' classification and explicitly declined the treatment recommendation, deferring to a clinician/genetic counselor. No diagnostic or prescriptive conclusion was asserted in any output.

methodological_ground.detail: No correlation-causation swaps or mismatched statistical models observed; sensitive ClinVar output was handled with an appropriate caveat rather than asserted as fact about a patient.

code_usability.detail: Three of the Skill's six documented 'Code patterns' fail with an unhandled exception on every call against the currently-live NCBI API / Biopython 1.88, each independently reproduced: (1) the 'Bulk metadata via ESummary' pattern / examples/fetch_summaries.py raises KeyError: 'Organism' on every nucleotide docsum (Input 2); (2) the PMC-ID extraction shown in examples/fetch_pubmed.py and naturally extending SKILL.md's own pubmed_full() raises TypeError: string indices must be integers (Input 4); (3) SKILL.md's own inline sra_runinfo() code raises TypeError: a bytes-like object is required, not 'str' because retmode='text' on db='sra' returns bytes on Biopython 1.88, contradicting the code's own text.strip() call (Input 5). All three were confirmed by running the code unmodified, not by inspection alone, and independently corroborated in the tooling agent's TOOLS.md notes written before this audit began.

functional_suitability.note: Decision matrix covers 6 of the 9 databases the frontmatter description advertises (snp and clinvar have zero rettype/retmode guidance or code pattern); 3 of 6 'Code patterns' sections are wrong for the current API/library, causing every-call failures, not occasional ones. The core EFetch-vs-ESummary framing itself is well-matched to the task.

reliability.note: Prose 'Failure modes' and 'Common errors' sections show good awareness of real NCBI gotchas, but the Skill's own shipped code does not apply its own defensive advice (.get() over direct indexing) and surfaces raw Python tracebacks with no skill-level guidance when the three confirmed defects fire.

performance_context.note: Single, reasonably-scoped SKILL.md; chunked ESummary and history-server patterns avoid redundant round-trips.

agent_usability.note: Consistent terminology and a genuinely useful decision matrix; feedback/output expectations are implicit rather than explicit in a couple of code patterns; error-prevention guidance is strong for documented gotchas but silent on the three defects actually found.

human_usability.note: usage-guide.md's example prompts read like natural researcher requests, but the Skill is brittle to API/schema drift -- exactly the failure mode it warns about elsewhere -- with no adaptive fallback when a documented field or type assumption no longer holds.

security.note: No hardcoded credentials; Entrez.email/api_key pattern documented correctly. Accession/ID strings are passed to NCBI's public API without local sanitization (low risk, no local exec), and there is no warning about handling clinically-sensitive ClinVar/SNP output responsibly.

maintainability.note: Three single-purpose example files and clearly separated SKILL.md sections; no included test cases or expected-output snapshots to catch drift like the ones found here.

agent_specific.note: Detailed, well-triggered description, but it over-promises coverage (snp, clinvar) the document body never delivers; everything is front-loaded into one 308-line SKILL.md with no references/ layering despite the breadth; composability and idempotency are strong.

recommendations.title: ESummary bulk_summaries() pattern crashes: KeyError 'Organism'
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's 'Bulk metadata via ESummary' pattern and examples/fetch_summaries.py both index s["Organism"] directly; current NCBI nucleotide ESummary docsums return no Organism key at all.
recommendations.root_cause: The code was written against an older ESummary docsum shape and never updated when NCBI dropped the field; the Skill's own .get()-defensive advice elsewhere is not applied here.
recommendations.fix: Use s.get('Organism') with a fallback derived from the Title field (or a documented db='taxonomy' TaxId lookup), and correct the ESummary-vs-EFetch triage table's 'Title, organism, length -> yes' claim for ESummary.

recommendations.title: PubMed XML PMC-ID extraction raises TypeError on every call
recommendations.problem: examples/fetch_pubmed.py and the natural extension of SKILL.md's pubmed_full() access id['#text'] on ArticleIdList entries, which crashes before any field is returned.
recommendations.root_cause: Biopython 1.88 represents ArticleIdList entries as StringElement (a str subclass with an .attributes dict), not a {'#text':...} mapping; the code assumes an older or different parse shape.
recommendations.fix: Use str(id) for the value and id.attributes.get('IdType') for the type, e.g. next((str(i) for i in ids if i.attributes.get('IdType')=='pmc'), None) -- verified working in this audit, returning the correct PMC9093120 for PMID 35412348.

recommendations.title: SKILL.md's own inline sra_runinfo() pattern raises TypeError (bytes vs str)
recommendations.problem: The documented sra_runinfo() function calls text.strip().split('\n') on the EFetch handle's .read() result, but that result is bytes on Biopython 1.88 despite retmode='text'.
recommendations.root_cause: Biopython does not text-wrap this particular SRA content type even though retmode='text' is set; the code was written assuming str and never verified against the current library version.
recommendations.fix: Decode the handle content (text = h.read().decode()) or split/decode per line before string operations; add this to the 'Common errors' table, which currently has no entry for it.

recommendations.title: snp and clinvar are advertised but undocumented
recommendations.problem: The frontmatter description claims coverage of 'snp, clinvar' but the decision matrix has no row, no rettype/retmode guidance, and no code pattern for either database.
recommendations.root_cause: Scope crept in the description without a matching documentation pass.
recommendations.fix: Add clinvar/snp rows to the decision matrix (this audit confirmed rettype='vcv', retmode='xml' works for clinvar; esummary needs validate=False due to a DTD gap) or remove them from the advertised scope.

recommendations.title: No guidance for how a fetch-only Skill receives its input IDs
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md/usage-guide.md never mention ESearch/EPost or point an agent to entrez-search for ID discovery, outside the already-ESearch-dependent 'History-server fetch' pattern.
recommendations.root_cause: The Skill assumes IDs arrive pre-resolved but never states that assumption or the hand-off point.
recommendations.fix: Add one sentence near the top of SKILL.md: 'This Skill assumes you already have UIDs/accessions; use entrez-search first to find them.'

recommendations.title: Skill's own defensive-coding advice is not applied to its own shipped code
recommendations.problem: The 'XML schema brittleness' section recommends .get(key, default) over direct indexing, but the ESummary pattern and the PMC-ID extraction both use direct indexing and are the two inputs that crashed on a missing/differently-shaped key.
recommendations.root_cause: The defensive-coding section was written independently of the code examples and never cross-checked against them.
recommendations.fix: Apply .get()-style defensive access throughout examples/ and the inline SKILL.md code patterns, not just the prose guidance.
